subject: Human Body
title: Glands: The Hormone Factories
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Glands: The Hormone Factories.

hook.text: Scattered across your body are small organs whose sole job is making hormones. These are endocrine glands.

buildup.text: Major glands include the pituitary, thyroid, adrenals, pancreas, and gonads. Each produces different hormone types.

twist.text: The gut is now considered the body's largest endocrine organ.

climax.text: Endocrine glands form a distributed network.

punchline.text: Your glands are a network, not a hierarchy. Each has a role.

quiz.question: What makes endocrine glands different from exocrine glands?
options: Endocrine glands release hormones directly into the blood without ducts
Endocrine glands are larger and more visible
Endocrine glands only function during puberty
